annotations.annotation_text: Page 584 opens Book 3, Chapter 4 ("The Bedroom Scene") during the Age of Men (closing) phase. This passage continues HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream, featuring HCE, ALP, Shem, Shaun, Issy. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 584 ("The Bedroom Scene"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men (closing) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind

annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "hen" on page 584 ("The Bedroom Scene"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
